[User #11744522692 postsDrat the Unimaginative【論語】陽貨第十七︰16Whirlpool Forums Addict] 83n D writes...
Shame they wont keep people in the loop regarding their Int'l packages.
I never had any trouble with getting automatically notified of tracking progress for parcels from Wiggle in the UK.
Many overseas retailers (Amazon, and ProBikeKit, among them) appear to have local shipping/forwarding agents that will process eParcel consignments on their behalf, and tracking by Australia Post effectively starts after the parcels have cleared Customs (even though there are recipient-viewable entries for when the consignments are registered with AP, prior to the parcels being physically in AP's possession).
[User #576927822 posts83n DMousse...schmousseWhirlpool Forums Addict] Drat the Unimaginative writes...
and tracking by Australia Post effectively starts after the parcels have cleared Customs
Really?
I spoke to Aus Post today and have spoken to them on Wednesday. No, that is incorrect. Tracking updates start after clearance. The first event however eg. "Arrived/processed at facility in AUSTRALIA" literally means nothing. Aus Post do not have the parcel. So where is it? Probably sitting in customs awaiting clearance.
Aus Post take possession of the parcel and push it out for delivery after clearance – only that part is true.
[User #11744522692 postsDrat the Unimaginative【論語】陽貨第十七︰16Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
83n D writes...
Tracking updates start after clearance. The first event however eg. "Arrived/processed at facility in AUSTRALIA" literally means nothing.
Actually, the first tracking event is when the consignment is electronically entered into AP's sytem, well before anyone at AP has seen or touched the parcel. That's why I said tracking effectively starts after the parcels have cleared Customs; prior to that, the tracking system simply does not have any clue where the parcels physically are at what time.
<EDIT> Here's a recent example of the detailed tracking information made available by Australia Post to me as the recipient, for an order I placed with ProBikeKit (in the UK):
Shipping information received by Australia Post 03:05pm Thu 26 Oct ALEXANDRIA NSW ‍ Shipping information approved by Australia Post 05:24pm Thu 26 Oct ALEXANDRIA NSW ‍ Processed through Australia Post facility 10:50pm Thu 26 Oct CHULLORA NSW ‍ Processed through Australia Post facility 03:10pm Fri 27 Oct SYDNEY NSW ‍ Awaiting Collection at ‹REDACTED› 04:47pm Fri 27 Oct SYDNEY NSW ‍ Delivered 04:33pm Mon 30 Oct SYDNEY NSW
Now, compare that to the detailed tracking information from OmniParcel, which is the UK delivery partner The Hut Group (which owns the ProBikeKit business) uses:
Friday, October 20, 2017 2:50 PM Tracking number allocated & WARRINGTON order ready ‍ Monday, October 23, 2017 8:42 PM Processed through Export Hub 10:54 PM International transit to GB, LHR destination country ‍ Thursday, October 26, 2017 1:56 PM Customs cleared AU 3:05 PM Manifest received ALEXANDRIA NSW Australia Post EParcel 5:24 PM Manifest accepted ALEXANDRIA NSW Australia Post EParcel 10:50 PM Processed at sortation facility CHULLORA NSW Australia Post EParcel ⋮

[User #654423792 postsgmailaccountWhirlpool Forums Addict] I purchased and lodged an express post satchel yesterday at Australia Post for a Sydney to Sydney delivery to a private address having heard about them now offering Saturday Delivery for such items.
After looking at the tracking details this morning it obviously isn't getting delivered today. I have since read that you need to apply a "Saturday" delivery sticker to the item for it to be delivered on Saturday.
1. Why would I not want an Express Post item to not get there as fast as possible? 2. Why did nobody at the post office notice express post item, local delivery when they were taking my payment for the satchel and scanning the item over the counter? 3. Why did I not remember that I'm dealing with a organisation that is corporately retarded and check for the inevitable 'gotchas'?
[User #77333535 postsMalichParticipant] Artstar writes...
Not entirely true. I've received a package via eBay's Global Shipping Programme. The moment FedEx handed it over to Australia Post here, I got a notification letting me know that my package was on its way to my Parcel Locker. I'd say they do keep people in the loop, where possible. It's not perfect but it's better than nothing at all.
Not always the case though, and not always that simple/obvious. Here's the short story of my latest GSP shipment (expected delivery 6/11 – 9/11)
Fedex Tracking: 27/10 – Picked up @ Erlanger GSP 5/11 – Arrived @ Matraville NSW. Received phone call from # which googles as "Fedex scam" ;) 6/11 – Status changed to "Clearance Delay". Contacted Fedex & gave them required info. 8/11 – Status still @ "Clearance Delay". Contacted Fedex again & gave them required info. 8/11 – Cleared Matraville NSW 9/11 – Arrived Brisbane Qld 9/11 – Emailed me saying it would be delivered by 6pm 9/11. Not delivered 11/11 – Emailed me again saying it would be delivered by 6pm 11/11 (Saturday). Not delivered. 13/11 – Fedex tracking status changed from "In transit"to "delivered" – backdated to 9/11. 13/11 – Contacted Fedex. Was told it had been passed to AusPost & they gave me tracking #
Auspost Tracking: 8/11 – Shipping info approved 9/11 – Processed through Chullora NSW 9/11 – Processed through Granville NSW 15/11 – Processed through [one of the Brisbane DCs] 15/11 – Delivered
So, no notification it had been handed to Auspost – in fact, Fedex pretended it was travelling in their network & they were delivering it until several days after they'd handed it to Auspost – and nothing from Auspost until it turned up (& yes, I am registered etc with them).
Not that I'm blaming Auspost for that – I blame Fedex for lying; if they'd just said in the tracking or the first 2 times I contacted them that it was being passed to Auspost in Sydney I wouldn't have had a problem with it – but you can't rely on either of them keeping you in the loop...
[User #38818213419 postsKalakIn the penalty box] Emmett T writes...
1. Why would I not want an Express Post item to not get there as fast as possible? Because it may be being sent to a business, or another address that won't be attended on a Saturday. They don't re-attempt delivery during the week, it's carded like any other missed article.
2. Why did nobody at the post office notice express post item, local delivery when they were taking my payment for the satchel and scanning the item over the counter? They don't care, nor should they decide if something needs Saturday delivery. If YOU need/want it, then you ask for it.
